evidence.quote: This demonstrates that even in the dense gas, star formation appears to be an extremely inefficient process.

findings_qualitative.value: Spectroscopic HCN/CO trends match cloud-scale CO imaging trends, so cloud properties vary with galactic environment

evidence.loc: Dense gas relations with environmental conditions

claims.hypothesis: Does the dense gas fraction proxy HCN/CO depend on local environment?
claims.experiment: Stacked HCN and CO in bins of Sigma_star, Sigma_mol and P_DE for 31 galaxies and fitted log-log relations with LinMix
claims.result: HCN/CO increases with all three quantities with slopes 0.48-0.65 and Pearson r 0.70-0.77
claims.finding: HCN/CO correlates strongly with surface density and pressure, so the physical state of molecular gas depends on environment

evidence.loc: Dense gas relations with environmental conditions
evidence.quote: We find strong correlations between the stacked HCN/CO and all three quantities, and anti-correlations between SFR/HCN and the same quantities

claims.hypothesis: Does the dense gas star formation efficiency proxy SFR/HCN vary with environment?
claims.experiment: Same stacks and LinMix fits for SFR/HCN
claims.result: SFR/HCN decreases with Sigma_star, Sigma_mol and P_DE with slopes -0.55 to -0.67 and larger scatter than HCN/CO
claims.finding: Dense gas appears less efficiently converted to stars in high-density, high-pressure regions, at face value

evidence.loc: Dense gas relations with environmental conditions
evidence.quote: At face value, this indicates that the denser molecular gas that effectively emits HCN is less efficiently converted to stars in high-surface-density, high-pressure parts of galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Is HCN luminosity a good predictor of SFR from cloud to galaxy scales?
claims.experiment: Gao-Solomon relation with a 31-survey literature compilation including ALMOND and EMPIRE
claims.result: Median SFR/HCN 1.3e-07 with 0.52 dex scatter, which grows from 0.27 dex (entire galaxies) to 0.70 dex (clouds)
claims.finding: HCN luminosity is a reasonable SFR predictor over ten orders of magnitude with significant scatter

evidence.quote: Overall, the literature compilation demonstrates that the HCN luminosity is a reasonable predictor of the SFR from cloud to galaxy scales across ten orders of magnitude.

claims.finding: Centres largely continue the disc trends, with speculative deviations at intermediate Sigma_star
